definition: The task of generating a novel image based on a natural language text description.
details: Text-to-image generation, powered largely by diffusion models conditioned on text embeddings, has enabled tools that let users create images from purely descriptive prompts without any artistic or design tools.

explainer.lead: Text-to-image generation creates a novel image from a natural language description. It matters because diffusion models conditioned on text embeddings let users produce images from purely descriptive prompts without artistic or design tools.

tiers.eli5: It is like describing a picture to an artist who paints it from your words alone.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers condition diffusion models on text embeddings to generate images from prompts. The pitfall is that the prompt only indirectly controls the output, so matching a precise description depends on how well the text embedding captures it.
tiers.paperLevel: Formally, a diffusion model generates an image conditioned on a text embedding, learning to denoise toward samples consistent with the prompt. The known limit is that control is mediated entirely through the text embedding, which bounds how precisely a description can be followed.

explainer.example: A user types a descriptive sentence and receives a new image matching that description, with no drawing tools involved.
